column1: # docs/findings_tags.tsv -- the classification of the findings of docs/FINDINGS.md that exp_soundness.py counts.

# One line per row of the table in FINDINGS.md:  id <TAB> layer[,layer] <TAB> effect <TAB> note (optional).   exp_soundness.py (and gate S51) refuse a finding without a line, and a line without a finding:
# a new finding is tagged when it is written.
#   kernel    the trusted C++ kernel: typing, conversion, admission, work budget, memoisation, the probe/rewind interface
#   tactic    the tactic layer, the unifier and the libraries (untrusted: the kernel checks every term they build)
#   engine    the learner's environment: engine, probe protocol, action language, term builder, search (untrusted)
#   data      the problem bank, recorder, dataset, hindsight, the synthetic generator and the semantic checks (untrusted)
#   pipeline  the training suite, the experiment tooling, estimates, documents
#   tooling   the mutation catalogue and driver, the repository layout, the gates
# EFFECT -- what it could do (one per finding)
#   accepts      trusted code accepted a term it must refuse (found in the baseline, in an earlier version of this kernel or in the checker)   <- the class that matters for soundness
#   refuses      trusted code refused, aborted on or mishandled a VALID input (fails closed: no false theorem, but a true one is lost)
#   wrong        untrusted code produced a wrong, ill-typed or misleading result, or failed on valid input (the kernel check refuses it, or a test caught it first)
#   resource     unbounded or excessive time or memory
#   data         the benchmark or the training data was wrong, duplicated or misleading
#   missing      a capability the platform needs did not exist yet (a design decision, not a defect of a released rule)
#   obligation   a soundness-critical rule that had to be designed or ported correctly (nothing wrong was released)
#   process      tooling, estimates, documents, the test harness itself
#   measurement  not a defect: a measurement recorded with the findings

# The tags are the author's reading of each row's text; where the row does not say which direction a defect went (accepted or refused) the less alarming reading is NOT assumed: the tag is `obligation` (F1, F24).
